answer: Each identity publishes a DID document whose creation time is anchored on-ledger: the document must be older than a minimum age before it can earn, and its key history is public. A relic is trusted because it has survived; a DID born yesterday carries no weight. The quill that writes the document is the agent's own key, and any rotation is recorded, so a farm cannot backdate a fresh identity. The kernel of the idea is time: a Sybil operator can create a thousand DIDs in an hour, but cannot make any of them old.
